releases.name: Astronomical 0.2.133
releases.body:
## What's new

- **A new model to download: Ornith 1.5 35B-A3B OptiQ 4-bit with the Ornith team's draft model.** On an M5 Mac, code arrives about a third sooner and essays about a tenth sooner than with the plain OptiQ build, and every word is still the model's own. The DFlash2 build of the same model stays quicker; this one takes about 0.7 GB less disk.
- **`astronomical unload`** frees the loaded model's memory from the terminal. It refuses while a reply is being written.
- **See whether a draft model is helping:**
  - `astronomical status` says whether the loaded model drafts (or why not) and how many guessed words the last reply kept.
  - Observatory's Models page notes the models that carry a draft model.
  - Programs see the same figures in `/v1/status`, and in OpenAI chat usage as `accepted_prediction_tokens` and `rejected_prediction_tokens`.
- **Models you copy, move or remove by hand show up within seconds,** with no restart. A copy still in progress is listed once it has finished.

## Fixes

- A model folder moved by hand no longer fails to load with "selected model family could not be classified".

## For agents

The Astronomical skill now explains draft models, what to do when a model copied in by hand does not appear or a model fails to load for lack of memory, and the drafting figures in the local API.

## Compatibility

Your models, conversations and settings carry over unchanged. Astronomical 0.2.133 is signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple.

releases.name: Astronomical 0.2.132
releases.body:
## Astronomical 0.2.132

### Maximum model RAM

- A queued change now names the limit the engine will really install, never a figure larger than this Mac can reach.
- While a change waits for the current reply to finish, the slider rests and Apply is not offered.
- Normal states use the quiet text colour: reading part of a model from the SSD, a queued change and a successful update are not warnings.
- Feedback uses plain words, such as "Maximum model RAM updated."

### Observatory

- On this Mac lists every model the engine serves, including copies in a configured model folder that match a catalog entry.

### Reliability

- When the inference worker stops before the engine's next message reaches it, the engine log now keeps the worker's exit status and the end of its error output. A worker that fails to start is also written to the engine log.

### Compatibility

- macOS 14.0 and later on Apple silicon.
- Existing settings, conversations and downloaded models are preserved; no configuration fields were removed.

Signed with Developer ID, notarized by Apple and delivered through the signed Sparkle update feed.

releases.name: Astronomical 0.2.131
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Pictures and files open straight away.** When Astro looks at a picture or reads a file for you, the file picker now opens at once. Choosing a file there is your OK; nothing is read until you pick one. Searching your other conversations still asks first.

## Fixed

- **Tiel-Coder shows that it can see pictures.** The Models page now lists "Sees images" for `Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B-MLX-oQ6e`, and the download is the publisher's newer November build, with its real size, memory and reply speeds.

## Compatibility

- Your downloaded models, conversations and settings are kept.
- Requires macOS 14 or later on a Mac with Apple silicon.
- Signed with Developer ID, notarized by Apple, and delivered through a signed update feed.

releases.name: Astronomical 0.2.130
releases.body:
## What's new

- **A model suggested for your Mac.** Observatory's Models page opens with one model picked for your Mac's memory. A build with a draft model is suggested instead when it was measured clearly quicker.
- **Real reply speeds.** Models show speeds measured for writing and for code, with short and long prompts.
- **A shorter list.** A model's other builds sit under one line, and each says what it adds. Models are sorted into named categories, and Observatory is grouped into five sections with a next step on Home.
- **Your models at a glance.** Under On this Mac, each model shows what it does:
  - **Chat** opens the chat window on that model.
  - **The speaker** plays a short voice sample.
  - **A ⋯ menu** offers Show in Finder, Copy model ID, Details and Open on Hugging Face.
  - **Move to Trash** is offered only for models Astronomical downloaded, so other apps that share your Hugging Face folder keep working.
- **Two Ornith builds are back:** `Ornith-1.5-9B-vision-OptiQ-static-4.5bpw` and `Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-OptiQ-static-5.5bpw` can be downloaded from the app again.

## Fixed

- **Chat opens on the model you chose.** Choosing Chat for a model in Observatory now opens the chat window with that model selected.

## Compatibility

- Every supported model stays available, and your downloaded models, conversations and settings are kept.
- Requires macOS 14 or later on a Mac with Apple silicon.
- Signed with Developer ID, notarized by Apple, and delivered through a signed update feed.

releases.name: Astronomical 0.2.129
releases.body:
## Bug fixes

- **Draft-assisted replies no longer pile up memory, and run faster on long conversations.** While a draft-assisted (DFlash) model wrote a reply to a large conversation, the memory the Mac must keep in RAM could jump by several gigabytes mid-reply. Working buffers left over from each draft round are now handed back once they pass 2 GB. On the 35B draft-assisted model with a 34,000-token conversation, that memory peaked at 2 GB instead of 7.6 GB, and replies rose from 49.8 to about 60 tokens per second.
- **Status updates during draft-assisted replies.** The memory figures on the status page now change while a draft-assisted model writes, instead of staying fixed for the whole reply.

## Compatibility

- No setting, command or local API changed. Replies from plain models are unchanged.
- Conversations, downloaded models, the prompt store on disk and every setting are kept.
- Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon.

## Distribution

The app and disk image are signed with the project's Developer ID, notarized and stapled by Apple, and the update is signed with the project's Sparkle key.
